19-01-opti-1: Sunrise in Florida. Light pours across the land.
19-01-opti-2: In the orange grove, every leaf turns to the sun.
19-01-opti-3: Down below, roots reach through the soil for water.
19-01-opti-4: Sunlight shines through a leaf. Something is happening in here.
19-01-opti-5: Zoom in. Tiny openings let air into the leaf.
19-01-opti-7: This sweet fruit is full of food the tree made itself.
19-01-opti-8: From sunlight, water, and air. But how?
19-01-opti-9: Let's find out how plants make their own food.
19-01-warm: A sunny new film today! Look closely at the young plant on the slab before we explain anything.
19-01-lesson: Today you're the crew's botanist. Follow water up a tree, test roots and leaves, and find out where a plant's food goes.
19-01-check: Three quick questions. It's not graded. It's just for you, so give each one your best try.
19-01-assign: Your turn to show how plants make food. Start with the sun, and follow it all the way to the fruit.
19-01-words: Photosynthesis. Sunlight. Energy. Leaf. Sugar. Roots.
how-19-01-compare: Drag the paper-towel strip under one tray and the dark paper under the other, or tap each one, then tap a tray. Press Turn on sun and water. Then swap them and press it again.
how-19-01-partc: Draw a before and after: one plant in bright sunlight and one plant kept in the dark. Under each one, write what you see. Name at least three differences in all.
